newsitem.title: GABON: Gabon ruling party heads for poll victory.
newsitem.headline: Gabon ruling party heads for poll victory.

text.p: President Omar Bongo's ruling party is headed for victory in Gabon's parliamentary polls held under a 1994 deal to defuse unrest that followed his disputed re-election, partial and unofficial results suggested on Friday.

But the main opposition National Woodcutters Rally (RNB), which won control of the capital Libreville during chaotic October municipal elections, has accused the authorities of deception in Sunday's poll.

Electoral officials say with results in from three of the former French colony's nine provinces, Bongo's Democratic Party has won 24 of the national assembly's 120 seats outright with one of its allies winning one.
The Woodcutters won two seats and an allied party one, they add.

"Landslide for the Gabonese Democratic Party, crushing defeat for the Woodcutters," the government daily L'Union trumpeted on Friday, saying Bongo's party had won 44 seats against six for the opposition.
It gave no breakdown of the opposition tally but said its unofficial results covered all nine provinces.

It did not make clear how many remaining seats would be contested in a December 29 second round but electoral sources said the ruling party was well-placed in many seats where it would contest a run-off.
"Bongo names his parliamentarians as he did in 1990," Le Bucheron, the Woodcutters weekly newspaper, had said on Thursday in an editorial tacitly acknowledging the trend.
"The problem is that multi-party politics, democracy do not rhyme with electoral nomination. That is why he uses electoral jiggery-pokery," it added.

Results from electoral officials showed the ruling party had won seven of 10 seats in Libreville, where the Woodcutters won the municipal polls and their leader Father Paul Mba Abessole is poised to become mayor. Abessole, a Roman Catholic priest, was runner up to Bongo in 1993.
More than 1,000 candidates were bidding for the 120 seats in the national assembly. Gabon, with just 1.2 million people, has an electorate of 550,000.
Problems with distribution of polling materials disrupted polling. The opposition says late delivery of voter cards and late posting of electoral lists contravened electoral law.

Bongo has ruled Gabon since 1968 and the death of Gabon's founding head of state, Leon Mba. Sunday's vote was Gabon's second multiparty legislative polls. The first were in 1990 when democratic reform swept Africa after the fall of Soviet-bloc communism.

Government and opposition set the timetable for the election in the 1994 Paris Accords agreed after more than a dozen people died in political and social unrest following Bongo's disputed re-election.
